title: models
universal_lens: Glicko-2 models skill as Gaussian latent variable with volatility-controlled variance; Dixon-Coles links scoring to Poisson processes with copula dependence; Bradley-Terry encodes pairwise comparisons via logit link; Conformal predictors yield finite-sample calibrated uncertainty sets.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference to update belief states over skill ratings and match outcomes using Glicko-2's Gaussian posteriors, Dixon-Coles' joint scoring probabilities, and Bradley-Terry's matchup likelihoods, with Conformal predictors ensuring coverage guarantees.
gse_mapping: GSE leverages state transitions in dynamic capability ratings (Glicko-2), exact score distributions (Dixon-Coles), and direct matchup odds (Bradley-Terry) to reason about situational contexts, while Conformal Margin Sets provide uncertainty quantification for decision-making under risk.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Glicko-2 model operates as a Bayesian filter updating skill estimates through match outcomes, incorporating time-based volatility decay. Its core equation maps posterior mean and deviation to prior inputs with outcome-dependent adjustments. The Dixon-Coles model extends standard Poisson to account for low-scoring dependencies via a copula correction factor ρ, enabling accurate modeling of rare events. Bradley-Terry uses a logit link to map unidimensional strength parameters into win probabilities, forming a kernel for pairwise comparisons. Conformal predictors invert model outputs into coverage-guaranteed prediction sets, offering robust uncertainty quantification. These primitives form a layered system where skill dynamics inform scoring models, which in turn feed into matchup logic, all wrapped in calibrated uncertainty bounds.
